risks.note: The BRSR identifies a complex and evolving regulatory environment across product, labour, environmental and corporate laws, which makes compliance critical for business continuity. Non-compliance would carry negative impact through penalties, litigation and operational disruption; mitigation is continuous monitoring of regulatory changes, internal audits, compliance training and strengthening governance frameworks.

Management lists regulatory energy efficiency norms among the key focus areas it tracks and mitigates. The portfolio is directly exposed to BEE star-rating and efficiency standard changes across fans, water heaters and pumps, which force re-engineering, re-rating and channel inventory transitions.

Compliance with product standards and growing demand for safe, innovative and sustainable products directly impact competitiveness; recalls or penalties carry negative impact while differentiation carries upside. Mitigation runs through strict quality controls, product testing, certifications and R&D investment in sustainable designs, supported by a stage-gate NPD framework, SAP Quality Module digitisation and QC Story projects.
risks.risk: Product quality, safety and sustainable product innovation

risks.note: Brand perception and customer trust are influenced by product quality, service experience, digital feedback and counterfeit risks. The exposure is visible in service load - the new CRM platform temporarily impacted daily call registration inflow and March 2026 saw a 51% increase in average daily call registrations versus the previous period, which increased open calls. Mitigation is stronger product quality and service standards, grievance redressal, brand monitoring and anti-counterfeit measures.
risks.risk: Brand reputation, customer trust and service quality

risks.note: Increased digitalisation exposes the Company to cyber threats, data breaches and misuse of confidential information, with negative impact from business disruption, data loss and remediation costs. Mitigation is robust IT security systems, access controls, cybersecurity audits, employee awareness and incident response plans.
risks.risk: IT security, data protection and cybersecurity

risks.note: Dependence on suppliers and ESG non-compliance in the supply base may disrupt production and damage reputation; mitigation is supplier diversification and ESG due diligence. Operationally the Company flags stock-out and excess-inventory risk, addressed through standardised SOPs, rigorous vendor onboarding, Butterfly warehouse integration, Project ForeSight forecast enrichment and QR-code Track-and-Trace across all product lines and 30 warehouses.

Unethical business practices can lead to reputational damage, legal consequences and loss of stakeholder trust. Mitigation is a strong code of conduct, whistle-blower mechanism, employee awareness and periodic internal reviews.

Permanent employee turnover was 28.60% in FY 2025-26 versus 26.36% in FY 2024-25, and permanent worker turnover rose to 50.21% from 4.00%, driven by 163 workers opting for a Voluntary Retirement scheme in September 2025. Sustained high churn raises the execution risk on capability-building programmes (CLDP, FLDP, ELDP, Grow with Crompton) and on field/channel continuity.
